setup.pitch: Briar Hollow is starving. A viable owlbear egg sits in the mayor’s bakehouse while half the village argues that it should be protected and the other half wants the largest omelet of their lives. Before the party can settle the vote, a gaunt male owlbear crashes into town in a hunger-mad rampage.
setup.gmSummary: Briar Hollow has roughly two and a half days of food left. The owlbear egg is alive and close to hatching. The father is starving and feverish; the party’s pooled one-day travel rations end his rampage immediately. If killed, his sick meat is useless and a mother roughly twice his bulk screams from the ridge. A self-proclaimed druid, Elmorrow Reed, argues passionately that the egg must be saved, but he is actually a beast broker for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie. Torren looks guilty first because he lied about finding the egg and used blankets and rope to move it, making him the red herring. A puzzle in Elmorrow’s wagon can expose the circus scheme before the final egg decision. If the egg survives, it hatches by the end and imprints on one player character.
setup.background: Three failed harvests and a washed-out bridge have left Briar Hollow on ration marks. Yesterday a charcoal burner found a warm owlbear egg in an abandoned poacher cart and carried it into town. The poachers are gone; the parent owlbears are not. The male has been scavenging because prey is scarce and recently ate from a diseased boar carcass. He follows food smell into the village, not malice. A traveler calling himself Elmorrow Reed arrived after hearing about the egg and presents himself as a druid. He is not one. He is a trained animal handler and broker for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie, hoping to obtain a live owlbear hatchling for profit.

quest.objective: Survive the father owlbear’s hunger-driven attack and decide the fate of the owlbear egg before nightfall.
quest.stakes: Briar Hollow may gain one communal meal, lose scarce food protecting a dangerous hatchling, provoke an enormous mother, or preserve a wild family at real cost to hungry people.
quest.deadline: Nightfall. The egg is close to hatching and the mother is moving somewhere beyond the ridge.
successConditions: The immediate owlbear attack ends and the village survives.
The party makes or enables a deliberate choice about the egg.
The consequences of that choice are made clear before the adventure ends.
failureConditions: The party abandons the village during the attack.
The egg is destroyed accidentally without anyone accepting responsibility for the consequence.

facts.text: Briar Hollow is genuinely short of food; the ration ledger is not a political trick.
The owlbear egg is viable, warm, and close to hatching.
The male owlbear is starving and feverish, not deliberately hunting villagers.
The party’s pooled one-day travel rations are enough to stop the father’s rampage; he eats and wanders away.
If the father is killed, his illness makes the carcass unsafe to eat.
A mother owlbear roughly twice the father’s bulk is nearby.
Elmorrow Reed is not a druid; he is a beast broker for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.
If the egg survives to hatch, the baby owlbear rapidly imprints on a nearby protector and follows that character.

secrets.text: Torren found the egg in a poacher cart, not an abandoned nest. Someone stole it before the village ever saw it.
secrets.revealCondition: Track the egg’s origin or get Torren talking privately.

secrets.text: Elmorrow carries a signed acquisition contract for one live juvenile owlbear and intends to sell or exhibit the hatchling.
secrets.revealCondition: Solve the wagon lock puzzle, find the hidden beast crate, expose his handler kit, or catch him trying to take the egg.

locations.name: Briar Hollow Square
locations.description: A muddy square between the bakehouse, granary, well, and six tight lanes. The owlbear egg rests in a padded bread trough inside the bakehouse.

locations.name: Village Granary
locations.description: Half-empty bins, ration stones on pegs, a locked salt chest, and a ledger with every household marked.

locations.name: Ridge Trail
locations.description: A wet deer path climbing through scrub oak toward an abandoned poacher cart and two sets of owlbear tracks.

locations.name: Broken Poacher Cart
locations.description: A collapsed axle, torn blankets, an empty egg cradle, old blood, and the remains of tainted boar bait.

locations.name: Mara’s Bakehouse
locations.description: Warm brick ovens, long tables, and the owlbear egg nested in blankets beside a cold mixing trough.

locations.name: Elmorrow’s Green Wagon
locations.description: A tidy green-painted wagon parked beyond the bakehouse. Bundles of herbs hang outside; beneath the tarp are reinforced cage fittings, a collapsible beast crate, and a brass-locked strongbox.

scenes.title: The Vote Before Supper
scenes.purpose: Put the egg, the hunger, and the moral split on the table before violence decides the question for them.
scenes.readAloud:
Briar Hollow smells like wet ash and thin soup. Forty-odd villagers crowd the square around a wooden bread trough padded with blankets. Inside it rests an egg larger than a keg, mottled brown and cream, warm enough to steam in the cold air.

Mayor Sella Vane raises both hands. “We have enough grain for days, not weeks. Mara says this is food. Torren says it is a child. I say we decide before hunger decides for us.”

From inside the egg comes one slow, heavy knock.

At the edge of the crowd, a moss-cloaked stranger raises a carved staff. “The old balance is plain,” he says softly. “The hatchling belongs with one who understands the wild.”
gmNotes: Do not make either side foolish. Mara wants to feed hungry children; Torren knows the egg was stolen from the wild.
Sella asks the party to investigate for one hour and then help the village choose.
The party can inspect the granary or follow Torren’s trail first. Both routes reconverge when the father attacks.
If they immediately vote to cook or spare it, Sella asks them to wait until the hour ends; the attack interrupts before the decision is carried out.

Elmorrow Reed introduces himself as a traveling druid. He is convincing but slightly too polished. Nature DC 12 notices his language is generic rather than technically druidic; this is suspicion, not proof.

scenes.title: Count What Is Left
scenes.purpose: Prove the starvation is real and quantify what the egg would actually change.
scenes.readAloud:
The granary looks full until Sella opens the good bins. Most are husks, seed grain, or mold-streaked sacks marked DO NOT EAT. A row of twelve clay ration stones hangs above the ledger. Only five remain on the left peg.

Mara taps the egg-weight column with one floury finger. “Cook it and everybody eats once. One proper meal. Tomorrow we are hungry again.”
gmNotes: Puzzle: the ration board uses one stone per communal half-day. Five stones means about two and a half days at current rationing.
Investigation DC 12 verifies the ledger and reveals Sella’s household has taken less than its allotment, not more.
The egg could provide one full village meal plus broth; it cannot solve the famine.
A crash and screaming from the square ends this scene when the table is ready: the father has arrived.

scenes.title: What Followed the Cart
scenes.purpose: Reveal the egg was stolen, the father is scavenging, and a vastly larger mother is somewhere nearby.
scenes.readAloud:
The trail ends at a cart with one wheel folded under it. A nest of torn blankets lies in the bed, still holding bits of shell-colored down. Around the wreck are two kinds of tracks: one broad as a dinner plate, the other so large your boot fits inside the pad without touching the edges.

Beside the ditch, flies worry at a half-eaten boar carcass streaked with dark bile. The smaller owlbear tracks circle it again and again, then stagger downhill toward Briar Hollow.
gmNotes: Nature or Survival DC 12: the smaller adult fed here recently and is moving badly, as if sick or starving.
The huge tracks belong to the mother and are roughly twice the father’s bulk. Do not stage her as a fair combat encounter.
Torren admits the egg was already in the poacher cart; the village did not steal it from a nest directly, but keeping it still keeps stolen property.
A hunter’s snare crosses the return path. Resolve the hazard, then the village bell rings three times: attack.

RED HERRING: Torren’s bundle contains cut rope, stained blankets, and a hooked woods knife. It looks like poaching gear, but it is exactly what he used to carry the egg from the wreck. Insight DC 12: his guilt is about bringing the egg home, not selling it.

scenes.title: The Hungry Father
scenes.purpose: Make the party choose between spending their own food and solving the immediate danger with violence.
scenes.readAloud:
A wall of feathers and fur slams through the smokehouse door. The owlbear that stumbles into the square is huge, but it is not healthy. Its ribs show under patchy feathers. Foam ropes from its beak. It swats a rain barrel aside and wheels toward the smell of food.

People scatter. The creature rears, shrieks, and charges the long table where the village’s supper — and your own travel packs — have been thrown together.
gmNotes: The party has a simple noncombat answer: offer their pooled one-day travel rations. No check. The father stops attacking, eats everything offered, and wanders back toward the ridge.
If they need to move close enough safely, Animal Handling DC 12 lets one character place food without drawing an opportunity attack; throwing the food from 20 feet works automatically.
If they fight, use the Owlbear Father quick-run block. He fights in panic until dropped or fed.
If killed: Medicine or Nature DC 10 shows fever, gut lesions, and black bile. The carcass is unsafe; the meat cannot feed the village.
If killed, immediately read the mother consequence: from the ridge comes a deeper answering scream, and birds rise from trees around something twice his bulk.
If fed, villagers see the same animal they called a monster choose food over blood. That should affect the final debate, but not dictate it.
Elmorrow urges the party not to kill the father because a surviving parent makes the egg easier to market as a 'rescued family story.' He never admits that reason.

scenes.title: The Druid’s Locked Wagon
scenes.purpose: Pay off the Torren red herring, give the table a real puzzle, and expose Elmorrow’s circus scheme before the final decision.
scenes.readAloud:
Elmorrow’s green wagon smells of mint, cedar oil, and something medicinal. The outside looks like a traveling healer’s cart. Under the rear tarp, however, iron anchor rings are bolted through the floor.

A brass strongbox sits beneath the bench. Its lid has four sliding picture tiles: an egg, a chain, a striped circus tent, and a silver coin. Scratched into the lid is a sing-song couplet:

“Shell before shackle, shackle before show; show before silver — that’s how fortunes grow.”
gmNotes: This is a player puzzle first, not a roll. Correct order: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN.
Solving it opens the strongbox and reveals a Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie contract purchasing one live juvenile owlbear, a brass handler token, and measured sedative packets.
The contract proves Elmorrow is not a druid. It names him as an animal acquisition agent.
If players force the box instead: thieves’ tools DC 13 or Strength DC 14. Failure makes noise and brings Elmorrow running, but the evidence remains obtainable.
Torren’s rope and blankets do not match the wagon hardware. This is where the red herring cleanly collapses.
If confronted, Elmorrow tries to talk his way out, then flee. He is not intended as a boss fight.

scenes.title: Egg, Oven, or Woods
scenes.purpose: Force the actual moral decision after the easy assumptions have been stripped away.
scenes.readAloud:
The egg knocks again from inside the blanket trough. This time a hairline crack runs across one end.

Mara has a cleaver on the table, not in her hand. Torren has a carrying sling ready. Elmorrow stands beside the door with his green wagon already hitched.

Mayor Sella looks at you instead of any of them. “Now we know what it costs,” she says. “And now we know who has been lying. Choose what we are willing to pay.”
gmNotes: Cook it: one full village meal tonight and broth tomorrow morning. The mother will still be searching. No one gets to pretend the meal solved the famine.
Let it hatch: Mara agrees only if the hatchling is kept outside the houses. It will need scarce food immediately. The village accepts that cost because the party chose it.

Return it to the wild: Torren knows a sheltered ravine near the poacher cart. If the father was fed, his tracks lead that way. If he was killed, the mother’s scream makes the trip frightening but still possible; do not force a boss fight.
Any creative solution is legal if it accepts both halves of the problem: hungry people and a dangerous living animal.
The egg begins hatching during the debate if the table stalls; this creates urgency, not a forced answer.

If Elmorrow was not exposed in the wagon, he makes one final push to take custody. A character who challenges him can notice the reinforced crate, sedative kit, or circus token without solving the puzzle; the twist should not be permanently missable.

If the egg survives this scene, it begins hatching before the resolution. The baby imprints on the character holding, feeding, protecting, or soothing it. If no one clearly qualifies, randomly select one player character.

scenes.title: What Hunger Remembers
scenes.purpose: Give a clear finale/resolution, state the cost plainly, and leave the village changed rather than morally graded.
scenes.readAloud:
Night settles over Briar Hollow. Somewhere beyond the ridge, something enormous calls once into the dark.

In the village, bowls are filled or left empty. A shell is cracked, carried, or kept warm. Nobody cheers. Nobody calls the choice easy.

Mayor Sella closes the ration ledger. “Tomorrow,” she says, “we live with what we decided tonight.”
gmNotes: Pick the ending matching the table’s actual choice. Do not declare a moral winner.
If the father died, include the mother’s distant scream in every ending. The threat is a consequence, not an automatic sequel fight.
If the father lived, Torren can follow his tracks at dawn. This may make returning the egg easier later.
Reward practical help: Sella pays what little coin the village can spare and gives a community favor rather than treasure that would trivialize the hunger.
BABY OWLBEAR END BEAT: if the egg survived, hatch it now. Imprint on the PC who most clearly protected/fed/soothed it; if unclear, roll randomly among the PCs. The bond is not magical.
If Elmorrow escaped, he can remain a future nuisance; do not let him steal the baby off-screen after the players earned the ending.

encounters.name: Starving Owlbear Father
encounters.summary: A gaunt feverish owlbear attacks the food table in a hunger-mad panic.
encounters.resolution: Feed the party’s pooled one-day rations, drive him off, or defeat him.
encounters.talkOut: No speech is needed. Offering the party’s pooled one-day rations ends the attack automatically: he eats and wanders into the woods.
encounters.bypass: Throw the pooled rations 20 feet away from villagers. He follows the food and disengages from the fight.
encounters.special: If killed, his meat is unsafe. His death triggers the distant scream of the mother owlbear, roughly twice his bulk.

puzzles.name: Five Stones on the Ration Board
puzzles.prompt: Twelve clay stones once hung over the ledger. Five remain on the left peg. A chalk note says: ONE STONE = ONE HALF-DAY FOR ALL FORTY-TWO.
puzzles.solution: Five stones equal two and a half days of village food at current rationing. The egg adds roughly one communal meal, not a lasting solution.
puzzles.failForward: If the players do not solve or care about the count, Mara explains it plainly. The moral choice continues with the same facts.

puzzles.name: Shell Before Shackle
puzzles.prompt: Four sliding tiles on the brass strongbox show an EGG, a CHAIN, a CIRCUS TENT, and a SILVER COIN. The scratched rhyme reads: “Shell before shackle, shackle before show; show before silver — that’s how fortunes grow.” Arrange the four tiles.
puzzles.solution: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN. The lock clicks open, revealing the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie acquisition contract, handler token, and sedatives.
puzzles.failForward: Thieves’ tools DC 13 or Strength DC 14 opens the box. On a failed attempt Elmorrow arrives and tries to stop them, exposing enough of the crate and paperwork that the investigation still moves forward.

traps.name: Poacher’s Leg Snare
traps.trigger: A creature crosses the concealed wire on the return path from the poacher cart.
traps.effect: On a failure, the creature is yanked prone and restrained 10 feet up by the ankle. Escape DC 12 Strength or Dexterity; cutting the rope also works.
traps.purpose: Fail-forward: the village alarm bell begins while the trapped character is being freed; the party still reaches the attack.

items.name: Living Owlbear Egg
items.description: A keg-sized warm mottled egg, close to hatching.

items.name: Party’s One-Day Travel Rations
items.description: The party’s pooled one-day travel food. Offering all of it to the father owlbear ends his attack with no check.

events.name: The Mother Answers
events.effect: If the father dies, a deeper owlbear scream rolls from the ridge and something roughly twice his bulk moves behind the tree line.

events.name: The Baby Chooses
events.effect: If the egg survives to hatch, the baby owlbear imprints on the player character who most directly held, fed, protected, or soothed it. If that is unclear, randomly select one player character. The bond is behavioral, not magical.

endings.name: The Largest Omelet in Briar Hollow
endings.condition: The village cooks the viable egg.
endings.result: Everyone eats one full meal. The famine is not solved. If either parent lives, the wild family continues searching for the missing egg. The village remembers that the party chose people first.

endings.name: Let It Hatch
endings.condition: The village keeps the egg warm and accepts the hatchling.
endings.result: A hatchling emerges outside the houses. Feeding it immediately costs scarce food. Torren takes responsibility for moving it away from homes as soon as it can travel. The village remembers that the party chose a life they did not create. Before the scene closes, the egg hatches. The baby owlbear imprints on the PC who most directly protected or soothed it; if unclear, choose a random PC. It follows that character, cries when separated, and treats them as its parent.

endings.name: Back to the Ridge
endings.condition: The party carries the egg to the sheltered ravine near the poacher cart.
endings.result: The egg leaves the village food supply untouched. If the father was fed, his tracks eventually join the route. If he was killed, the mother’s distant cry follows the party but no forced boss fight occurs. The village stays hungry but ends the night without owning the egg. Before the scene closes, the egg hatches. The baby owlbear imprints on the PC who most directly protected or soothed it; if unclear, choose a random PC. It follows that character, cries when separated, and treats them as its parent.

endings.name: Not the Village’s Choice
endings.condition: The party takes responsibility for the egg and leaves with it.
endings.result: Briar Hollow neither eats nor raises it. The party inherits the problem: a near-hatching owlbear egg, a hungry road, and perhaps a mother searching behind them. Before the scene closes, the egg hatches. The baby owlbear imprints on the PC who most directly protected or soothed it; if unclear, choose a random PC. It follows that character, cries when separated, and treats them as its parent.

endings.name: Broken in the Panic
endings.condition: The egg is destroyed accidentally during violence or flight.
endings.result: Nobody gets a meal and no hatchling survives. Sella records the loss without pretending it was a choice. If the father died too, the mother’s cry is the last sound over the village.

recovery.principle: No single NPC or investigation scene is required. Preserve the hunger facts and the egg choice; change delivery, not truth.
policies: Required facts may move to physical evidence or another NPC if a scene is skipped.
The father’s food solution remains available until he is dead.
The ending is never locked by a failed check; the cost may increase, but the table still chooses the egg’s fate.

routes.trigger: Sella refuses, is unavailable, missing, or dead
routes.response: Her ration ledger and five clay stones remain in the granary. Mara can call a village vote.

routes.trigger: The father is attacked or killed before anyone understands his hunger
routes.response: His emaciation, fever, black bile, and the tainted boar evidence reveal the same truth afterward. If alive, thrown rations can still end the fight.

routes.trigger: The party bypasses or skips the granary or ridge trail
routes.response: Move the missing required facts into the attack scene: villagers shout the ration count, and the father’s condition is obvious at close range. Huge mother tracks are found at the square edge afterward.

routes.trigger: The party leaves town with the egg before the attack
routes.response: The father follows the smell of their packs and egg on the ridge road instead of entering the square. Run scene-father there, then let them decide whether to return, hatch, or carry the egg onward.

routes.trigger: The party skips or bypasses Elmorrow’s wagon puzzle
routes.response: At the final egg debate Elmorrow’s reinforced beast crate, Moonpetal token, and sedatives become visible when he rushes to take custody. The same truth is delivered without requiring the puzzle.

pathPressure.principle: Prepared pays. Rush costs. The ending is never locked; they still finish.

prepared.payoff: They know exactly what cooking the egg buys and can stop false claims during the final debate.
They know the father is sick and the mother is enormous before the attack; Nature/Medicine checks on the father have advantage.
They enter the final debate knowing the self-proclaimed druid is a circus broker and can prevent him from manipulating the village.

rushed.cost: The father attack begins with villagers packed around the food table; the first round is chaotic and the party learns the truth under pressure.
The carcass is unusable and the mother’s scream becomes an immediate consequence before the egg decision.

rushed.when: They trust Elmorrow without checking his wagon
rushed.cost: He reaches the final debate with social credibility and tries to take immediate custody of the hatching owlbear.

notDeviation: Cooking the egg is not failure.
Sparing the egg is not success by itself.
Any ending is valid if the party understands the cost.

oneshotRecipe.tale: A starving village and a living egg

rooms.note: Shell → chain → tent → coin exposes the fake druid
State the cost without judging it

notes: Use the SRD-style owlbear quick-run block supplied in this package. Feeding the pooled rations is an authored encounter resolution, not a spell or class feature.
Use the same encounter numbers for this adventure unless the table prefers a current SRD owlbear stat block. The authored feed-or-fight resolution is unchanged.

encounters.objective: End the father owlbear’s rampage without losing villagers.
encounters.start: He enters adjacent to the food table. Villagers flee; the party begins 20–30 feet away.
encounters.bypass: Throw the party’s pooled one-day rations at least 20 feet away from villagers. No check. He eats and wanders off.

creatures.name: Starving Owlbear Father
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +7 to hit, 1d10+5 piercing; Claws +7 to hit, 2d8+5 slashing.
creatures.trait: Keen sight and smell. Feverish Hunger: when the pooled one-day rations are offered, he immediately stops attacking, eats, and leaves the encounter.
creatures.tactics: Charges the nearest visible food before pursuing creatures. If attacked, defends himself normally. He does not coup de grace fallen villagers and will always choose offered food over another attack.

encounters.end: He is fed and leaves, is driven away, or is reduced to 0 HP. If killed, the carcass is unsafe and the mother screams from the ridge.

hazards.trigger: Cross the concealed poacher wire on the return path.
hazards.failure: Yanked prone and restrained 10 feet up by one ankle.
hazards.success: Step over the wire and point it out to the others.
hazards.failForward: Escape DC 12 Strength or Dexterity, or cut the rope. The village alarm bell starts while the party gets free.

rewards.when: The village survives the night and the party accepts responsibility for its decision.
rewards.reward: Sella gives 35 gp from the emergency strongbox and a standing Briar Hollow favor: food, shelter, or testimony when the village can provide it.

rewards.when: The party fed its own rations to the father.
rewards.reward: Mara replaces half the spent trail food from the bakehouse despite the shortage; the village publicly records the sacrifice.

rewards.when: The party returns the egg to the ridge.
rewards.reward: Torren gives a carved ashwood tracking charm worth 20 gp and advantage on one future local Survival check at the GM’s discretion.

features: two narrow lanes north toward ridge

cards.title: Baby Owlbear
cards.front: A damp, oversized owlbear hatchling with too-big paws, a snapping beak, and enormous yellow eyes.

rules: Tiny Beak: +3 to hit, 1 piercing damage.
Imprint: when it hatches, it bonds to the PC who most clearly held, fed, protected, or soothed it. If unclear, choose a random PC.
The bond is not magical. It follows that PC, cries when separated, steals food, and snaps at obvious threats.
Animal Handling DC 12 calms it for 1 hour.

cards.title: Starving Owlbear Father
cards.front: A gaunt adult owlbear with exposed ribs, ragged feathers, and foam around its beak.

rules: Multiattack: Beak +7, 1d10+5 piercing; Claws +7, 2d8+5 slashing.
Feverish Hunger: offer the party’s pooled one-day rations and he immediately stops attacking, eats, and leaves.
If killed, the meat is unsafe and useless.
His death triggers the distant scream of the mother owlbear.

cards.title: Mother Owlbear
cards.front: A scarred owlbear roughly twice the father’s bulk, visible only in pieces between the ridge trees.

rules: Multiattack: Beak +8, 1d10+5 piercing; two Claws +8, 2d8+5 slashing each.
Protect the Egg: she prioritizes reclaiming the egg or hatchling over killing characters.
Terrifying Charge: after moving 20 ft. straight toward a creature, DC 13 Wisdom or frightened until end of its next turn.
Use her as pressure, not a mandatory fair boss fight.

cards.title: Mayor Sella Vane
cards.front: A sleepless mayor gripping a ration ledger hard enough to bend its cover.

rules: Wants the village alive and the decision made honestly.
Knows the true ration count.
Secret: her own household has already gone to half-rations.
Voice: practical, counts before answering.

cards.title: Mara Dell
cards.front: A flour-dusted baker with a cleaver on the table and hungry children on her mind.

rules: Wants one full meal for the village tonight.
Knows cooking the egg does not solve the famine.
Not cruel; she simply ranks hungry people first.
Voice: blunt, uses kitchen measures.

cards.title: Torren Vale
cards.front: A soot-stained woodsman with cut rope, stained blankets, and exactly the wrong-looking knife.

rules: Looks like the poacher or seller.
Actually used the suspicious gear to carry the egg from the wreck.
Lied about where he found it because he knows bringing it home was reckless.
Insight DC 12: guilt, not greed.

cards.title: Elmorrow Reed
cards.front: A moss-cloaked 'druid' with polished nature sayings and a green wagon parked too close to the egg.

rules: Not a druid. Works for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.
Wants the hatchling alive for exhibition and sale.
Nature DC 12: his druid lore is shallow and rehearsed.
His wagon contains a beast crate, sedatives, handler token, and acquisition contract.
If exposed, he bluffs, then flees rather than fight.
